note: Maps each heading of docs/MANUAL.md to the evidence in this archive. `shelf` is catalogued (a named check backs what the section says), uncatalogued (built, not checked in the way the section describes) or none (the section describes no behaviour). `prs` give the state tag from gh. `gaps` names what the section says that no check covers. A heading of the manual missing here is shown as uncatalogued; a heading here missing from the manual fails the build.

sections.evidence: An overview. The status it states matches the front page: both versions play the slice, with no story or menu, and the cluck's sound on both.
The two subsections below.
`tools/build-web.sh` builds `dist/web` in the `parity` CI job, and headless Chromium loaded the served page for the screenshots of [chapter 4](chapter:m0-presenters#the-web-presenter-6).
sections.gaps: opening the page in a browser by hand; only headless Chromium has loaded it.

sections.evidence: `tools/build-dos.sh` writes `FIZZ2.EXE` and `CWSDPMI.EXE` to `dist/dos`, and `tools/check-dos.sh` runs them in headless DOSBox Staging ([chapter 4](chapter:m0-presenters#fizz2-exe-5)).
sections.gaps: js-dos, and a real 486 with a VGA display.

sections.evidence: On DOS, `tools/check-dos.sh` types Ctrl, Right, Right, Down and Esc with DOSBox's AUTOTYPE: the square moves (`MOVED yes`) and Esc ends `/LIVE` with status 0. The host tests `keen_layout_is_arrows_ctrl_alt_space` and `modern_layout_is_wasd_or_arrows_zxc` check every key of both layouts, and the decoder tests cover Z, X, C and both Ctrl and Alt keys, including that a Pause is never a Ctrl press. On the Web, headless Chromium was sent key events for both layouts over the DevTools protocol: the square moved, Ctrl and Z made it dash, and keys of the other layout did nothing.
sections.gaps: a real keyboard on either version; Pogo and Fire as live key presses on DOS, which only the replay feeds (as buttons); and Alt on DOS, which the smoke does not type.

sections.evidence: `tools/check-dos.sh` runs `/MODERN` (it moves on Z) and checks that the default Keen keys ignore W, A, S, D, Z, X and C. On the Web, headless Chromium toggled the Keys button, saw the hint change and the choice survive a reload.
sections.gaps: a browser where `localStorage` is blocked; the page is written to carry on without it, but no run covered that.

sections.evidence: `fizz-slice-view` tests pin the beak and caption pictures (open, shut between a double cluck's halves, bright, dark, blinking, captions off) and prove at every tick of the replay that a cluck changes only a beak patch and a caption box. `tools/check-dos.sh` runs `/NOCAPTIONS /MODERN` and the replay's golden `EVENT` lines name the chicken. Headless Chromium captured the Web page five ticks after a cluck, with the caption and the open beak. The DOS and Web caption shots at ticks 217 and 201 are in [chapter 9](chapter:slice), with the `cluck-path` diagram of what checks each step.
sections.gaps: the Captions button and the V key were not driven by a real key press or click, nor the localStorage round trip; a real DOS machine; the look of the words (judged from one screenshot).

sections.evidence: The page calls `navigator.keyboard.lock` on entering fullscreen where the API exists; headless Chromium reported the API present.
sections.gaps: everything the section promises about real browsers: fullscreen itself, Keyboard Lock holding Ctrl and Alt on a desktop, and the shortcuts (Ctrl+W, workspace shortcuts) that a tab cannot block. A headless browser shows none of these.

sections.evidence: `tools/check-dos.sh` runs the modes: `/REPLAY` must print the slice's golden transcript (`FINAL TICK 1268 HASH 0edebb797e63edff`) and `EXIT yes`, `/LIVE` must print `MOVED yes` and `VECTORS RESTORED yes`, `/BENCH` (run at a fixed 26,800 cycles) must print positive step and drawing averages, the slice's final hash and `EXIT yes`, `/PROBE` must print the `PROBE` lines each of 21 DOSBox configurations expects and a `CELLS` hash equal to the host's, `/CHECKCELLS` must print the 4,000 bytes read back from video memory equal to the host builder's for six machines (colour, EGA, CGA, Hercules), a host test fails if any script runs the interactive `/CHECK`, and `/PANIC` must exit with status 3 ([chapter 4](chapter:m0-presenters#fizz2-exe-5)).
sections.gaps: the 30-second limit of `/LIVE` and its final-tick line: a capture run printed `LIVE TICKS 1800` (30 seconds at 60 a second), and no committed check asserts it; and that `/REPLAY` takes about 21 seconds, which the BIOS tick bound of 383 to 387 covers only as a count. The `/BENCH` figures are DOSBox's and say nothing certain about a real 486. The `/CHECK` screen itself (keys, Enter on to `/LIVE`) is never run by a check and was not driven by hand here. The `/PROBE` results are DOSBox's too: no real machine, and no monochrome VGA or missing maths chip, has been probed.

sections.evidence: `tools/check-dos.sh` runs `FIZZ2.EXE` in headless DOSBox with `/?`, `/HELP`, `/help`, `-?`, `/? /LIVE`, `/MODERN /HELP /PANIC` and `/? /BOGUS`; each must exit 0 and print exactly the text of `crates/fizz-machine/tests/help.txt` and none of the lines a played or hooked run prints. `/BOGUS` and `/LIVE /MUSIC:FOO` must exit with status 2 and name the switch. The help and the argument parser both read one table in `fizz-machine` (`switches.rs`); host tests fail if a recognised switch has no help line or a help line names no switch, if the text is over 25 lines, 79 columns or plain ASCII, or if it differs from the golden file.
sections.gaps: a real DOS console: the help was read only from DOSBox's redirected output, so how the 25 lines look on a real 80 by 25 screen, and whether COMMAND.COM on FreeDOS passes `/?` through to the program rather than answering it, are unchecked.

sections.evidence: `tools/check-dos.sh` runs `/PROBE` under sb16, sb1 and no sound card with each flag and with planted version 1, version 2 and damaged `FIZZ2.CFG` files, and compares the whole `SOUND` line, including the fallback and file-problem words. It checks that a run with flags leaves the file as it was, that `/CFGTEST` saves the documented 9 bytes and reads them back, and that `/LIVE` prints the line. It runs `/REPLAY` under eight combinations of file and flags and requires the golden `TICK`, `FINAL` and `EVENT` lines every time. `fizz-machine` tests cover the file's round trip, the version 1 upgrade, every kind of corruption and the flag precedence.
sections.gaps: a real machine: every run is DOSBox's, so whether the chosen device is the one you would hear is unchecked (the `AUDIO` line only shows which path wrote); the file on a real disk, for example read-only media.

sections.evidence: `fizz-machine` tests cover the governor over synthetic costs: cheap frames stay at 60, 120% goes to 30, 180% keeps the rate, 200% and under 67% go to 60, the edges of each band, a window of exactly 32 frames, fixed modes that never change, and a draw on every second tick at 30. `tools/check-dos.sh` runs `/REPLAY` under `/FPS30` (635 pictures for 1,268 steps), `/FPS60` (1,269), the default Auto at 26,800 cycles (stays at 60) and Auto at 4,500 cycles, where a picture costs about 125% of a sixtieth of a second (ends at 30); every run must print the golden `TICK`, `FINAL` and `EVENT` lines. It plants `FIZZ2.CFG` files with each frame-rate byte and a bad one, runs `/LIVE` with and without a flag over them, checks the `FRAMES` line's rate and mode and the half-as-many pictures at 30, and checks the file is never changed or created by a flag.
sections.gaps: how 30 looks and feels: nobody has judged the steppier movement; a real 486, where the cost of the ISA VGA copy, the retrace wait and the x87 is unmeasured, so Fizz 1's thresholds have not been tuned for Fizz 2; and Auto in `/LIVE` on a slow machine, which the committed checks cover in `/REPLAY` only (a `/LIVE` run at 4,500 cycles by hand ended at 30).

sections.evidence: `tools/check-dos.sh` runs `/REPLAY` under an OPL3 Sound Blaster (Auto and `/SB`), a Sound Blaster Pro 2, an OPL2 Sound Blaster, `oplmode opl2` on a Sound Blaster 16, an AdLib-only machine, `/MUSIC:SB /FX:ADLIB` (an OPL3 carrying the channel-5 effect through the OR rule), `/SPEAKER`, no card and `/NOSOUND`. Every run must print the golden `TICK`, `FINAL` and `EVENT` lines, `BIOS TICKS` inside the bound and `VECTORS RESTORED yes`, and the `AUDIO WRITES <n> SPEAKER STEPS <m>` line must show writes on a chip, steps on the speaker and zeros for both when silent. A `/PANIC` run on an OPL3 with a cluck sounding exits 3. `fizz-sfx` and `fizz-machine` tests cover the players and the OR rule on the host. A DOSBox recording of the three paths is not silent and the `/NOSOUND` one is. The `cluck-path` diagram in [chapter 9](chapter:slice) shows each box of the DOS path with its check; its last box, a real chip or speaker, has none.
sections.gaps: how any of it sounds: nobody has listened on DOSBox or anywhere else, and a real OPL2, OPL3, Sound Blaster or PC speaker has not been tried (the register write timings are Fizz 1's, unmeasured here); that the chip really leaves OPL3 mode and goes quiet on exit and panic, which a headless run cannot hear; and the cost of the 560 Hz interrupt on a 486, which `/BENCH` (still at 60 Hz) does not include.

sections.evidence: `tools/check-dos.sh` runs `/REPLAY` in headless DOSBox and compares its `TICK` and `FINAL` lines with the slice's golden transcript, so the DOS rules, level and hash match the native build, and asserts `EXIT yes`. The picture is the one `fizz-slice-view` draws, pinned by frame digests at six ticks of the replay, and the HUD strip is tested in `fizz-present-dos` (`the_slice_hud_shows_ammo_key_deaths_and_tick`). The screenshot is a real DOSBox Staging grab of `/REPLAY` under a virtual X server.
sections.gaps: playing it by hand: `/LIVE` was exercised only by AUTOTYPE key presses, so how the camera and the keys feel is unchecked; the picture on a real VGA screen and the speed on a real 486; and the sound, which no one has heard on a real machine.

sections.evidence: `tools/check-parity.sh` runs the 1,268-tick slice replay inside the built WASM module under Node or Bun and compares every `TICK`, `FINAL` and `EVENT` line with `crates/fizz-ep2/slice-replay.txt`, and the `App` host tests step the same script through the Web presenter's pacer and key latch and compare its hash with the rules after every tick. Headless Chromium loaded the built page, drew the level, moved Ben on real key events in the Keen layout and fired a shot (`AMMO` fell to 4). The screenshot is of that build. The `capture-web.py` screenshots play the golden replay's keys one tick at a time against a fake clock, so each shot is a state of the replay.
sections.gaps: a person playing it; the Modern layout on this page, which headless Chromium was only partly sent; the look of the level, which is a first drawing; and any real display scaling.

sections.evidence: The level's tests in `fizz-ep2` check its size, the named places and that the door starts closed; the replay climbs from the spawn through the door to the exit, which `check-dos.sh` repeats on DOS (`EXIT yes`). The colours are the `tile_colour` table of `fizz-slice-view`, with a test that the tile types have distinct colours.
sections.gaps: that the level is pleasant to play; the colour names in the section were read from the code and the screenshot, not checked by a test.

sections.evidence: Walking, jumping with a cut, the pogo and its held high bounce and the stun shots are proved bit for bit against Fizz 1's golden traces (`tests/fizz1`), and the slice replay uses them. The key mapping of both layouts is tested in `fizz-present-dos`. Look and aim are proved against Fizz 1 by the `look` and `aim` traces ([chapter 8](chapter:rules)), which hold the look timers and the aim bit for bit; the manual's 0.2 second wait and 3.6 tile reach are the constants those rules use. The DOS look and aim screenshots were typed into DOSBox through the X server ([chapter 9](chapter:slice)).
sections.gaps: the Alt key on DOS, which the keyboard smoke does not type, and the pogo and Fizz keys in a live DOSBox session (the replay feeds them as buttons, not as key presses); the feel of the look's slide, and the first shaft's floor, where the manual says the view cannot slide, which no test names

sections.section: The red key and the door
sections.evidence: `the_script_exercises_every_rule_of_the_slice`, `the_door_stays_shut_without_the_key`, `an_open_door_survives_a_death_and_the_key_does_not` and `a_lost_key_comes_back_with_the_respawn` in `fizz-ep2`, and the `key_door` trace against Fizz 1. The replay on DOS opens the door.

The `gloop_patrol`, `stomp`, `stomp_pogo` and `fizz_stun` traces against Fizz 1; the replay stuns the chicken once by a shot and once by a stomp. A test in `fizz-slice-view` checks that a stunned chicken is drawn differently from a walking one. The stun stars are Fizz 1's two 16 by 8 sprites drawn 0.3 tiles above a stunned chicken, swapping every 10 ticks; the pinned frame at tick 700 of the replay shows them, on both presenters. A DOSBox grab of `/REPLAY` and a headless Chromium frame at tick 300 show them ([chapter 9](chapter:slice)).
sections.gaps: the look of the chicken (a placeholder) and its flashing, which are drawn in the code and seen in a screenshot only; the stars twinkling in motion on a real display, which nobody has watched on DOS

sections.evidence: The replay dies once on the spikes carrying the key, and `the_script_exercises_every_rule_of_the_slice` checks that the key drops, the ammo refills and the door switch resets; `check-dos.sh` repeats the run on DOS. The shake is a view effect from a baked table of at most one pixel for 18 ticks, derived from Ben's `dead` timer; the pinned frame at tick 400 is a death frame, and a test checks that the shaken camera still clamps to the map. The hash, the events and the DOS frame digests of other ticks are unchanged by it.
sections.gaps: the look of Ben's tumble, which uses a borrowed pose because the first game has no dead pose; the shake itself: a shift of at most a pixel cannot be seen in a still, and nobody has looked at it on DOS in DOSBox or on a real display

sections.evidence: The replay test `the_script_exercises_every_rule_of_the_slice` plays the level through the key, the chicken, the door and the exit, and the level's own tests lock its tiles; the Fizz 1 traces `key_door`, `gloop_patrol`, `stomp`, `fizz_stun` and `route` match bit for bit.
sections.gaps: how the level reads to a first-time player, and whether the door and key are easy to find.

sections.section: Moving, jumping, the pogo stick and the blaster
sections.evidence: Walk, jump, the cut jump, the pogo and its held bounce are the golden Fizz 1 traces `run`, `jump_full`, `jump_cut`, `pogo_idle` and `pogo_held`, compared bit for bit by `tests/fizz1_traces.rs`; the shots are the `fizz_stun` trace and the replay.
sections.gaps: how the keys feel on a real keyboard.

sections.section: Death and respawn on the Web
sections.evidence: The replay dies once on the spikes carrying the key; `an_open_door_survives_a_death_and_the_key_does_not` and `a_lost_key_comes_back_with_the_respawn` check what a death keeps and what it resets, and `the_script_exercises_every_rule_of_the_slice` checks the ammo.
sections.gaps: the fall off the bottom of the level and the exact length of the death pause on a real display.

sections.evidence: Headless Chromium read the seven lines from the page: they start at `TICK 0` and change as Ben moves, `AMMO` fell to 4 after a shot, and Restart returned the tick to the start. The values come from the `App` getters the host tests read. Headless Chromium took screenshots of the filled page at 960 by 540, 390 by 780 and 1600 by 520, each 13 tiles tall with the width following the window, and the page's `HASH` at tick 300 equals the golden transcript's `TICK 300` line ([chapter 9](chapter:slice)).
sections.gaps: `KEY`, `DOOR` and `EXIT` changing in the browser: the replay reaches all three in the host tests, but no browser run has played that far; the panel opened with `H` or the `?` button, which no run pressed, and a real window being resized or a phone being turned

sections.evidence: `web/sfx.test.ts` runs the real Undertone against a recording stand-in for `AudioContext` under `bun test`: each of the four variants schedules the voices of `assets/sfx/cluck.ts`, nothing plays before unlock, while muted, on a hidden tab or past four simultaneous clucks, and blocked storage does not break mute. `tools/check-web-sfx.py` drives the built page in headless Chromium with the same kind of stand-in: no context and no sound before a key press, the cluck at tick 197 scheduling variant 2 after one, `M` muting, and the choice surviving a reload. The `App` host tests check that no cluck is lost when a frame runs several ticks. The `cluck-path` diagram in [chapter 9](chapter:slice) shows each box of the Web path with its check.
sections.gaps: how any cluck sounds: nobody has listened, and a stand-in cannot hear. Also the first-key start under each real browser's autoplay policy, the hidden-tab silence in a real browser, and the pile-up cap against real overlapping clucks.

sections.evidence: The HUD's text is tested in `fizz-present-dos` and the picture is pinned by frame digests in `fizz-slice-view`; the hash is the parity gate's, equal on native, Web and DOS ([chapter 5](chapter:parity)); 60 steps a second is the pacer of `fizz-hal` and the timer of [chapter 3](chapter:m0-core#the-60-hz-timer-that-keeps-the-bios-clock). The Web lines are read from the `App` getters by the host tests.

Same moves, same `TICK` and `HASH`: the parity gate ([chapter 5](chapter:parity)), and the slice replay that `tools/check-dos.sh` and `tools/check-parity.sh` each compare with `crates/fizz-ep2/slice-replay.txt`.
sections.gaps: no check compares the two screens side by side: both call `fizz_slice_view::draw_slice`, so the picture is shared by construction, but the Web HUD is page text below the canvas while DOS draws it in the frame, and the Web build in a browser has not been played by a person.
